tips.title: En, au, aux for countries
tips.body: **En** for feminine countries: *en France*, *en Espagne*. **Au** for masculine: *au Portugal*, *au Pays de Galles*. **Aux** for plurals: *aux États-Unis*. Use **à** for towns: *à Paris*.

tips.title: After a negative, de replaces the article
tips.body: *Il y a une piscine* becomes *il n'y a **pas de** piscine*, not *pas une piscine*. The same happens with *du*, *de la* and *des*: they all collapse to **de**.

tips.title: Say how long and with whom
tips.body: A description question wants more than the place. Add the length of stay, who you went with and how you travelled: *j'y suis allé pendant une semaine avec ma famille en avion*.

tips.title: Let the gender pick the preposition
tips.body: Let the gender choose for you: feminine takes **en** (*en France*), masculine takes **au** (*au Portugal*), plural takes **aux** (*aux États-Unis*). The one to watch is a masculine country starting with a vowel, which takes **en** anyway — *en Iran*. Learn the gender with the country and the preposition follows.

why.matters: Where you go, who with, how, for how long and where you stay: every holiday description answers the same questions, and the exam's picture task and writing task ask them every year. The topic exists for the small words that carry the answers, *en* or *au* or *aux* before a country by its gender, *en* or *à* before a means of transport, *pendant* for how long, and the accommodation nouns with their verbs, *loger, louer, réserver*. *Y* returns to say *there*, and the negative *il n'y a pas de wifi* shrinks its article as it always does.

examples.title: En Espagne, au Portugal, aux États-Unis
examples.body: The preposition before a country is its gender wearing a hat: *en* for feminine countries, which is most of them, *au* for masculine, *aux* for plurals, *à* for a city. *Nous allons en Espagne, au Portugal, aux États-Unis, à Paris.* Coming back uses *de*, *du*, *des*. It is the same rule as the Francophone map from Year 9, and a run of right ones is what makes a holiday paragraph sound fluent.

examples.title: En avion, à vélo
examples.body: You travel *in* a vehicle you sit inside, *en avion, en train, en voiture, en bateau*, and *on* one you sit astride or use your own legs for, *à vélo, à pied*. English *by* covers both, which is why *par avion* is the error the listening paper hears. How long you spend is *passer*, *nous passons deux semaines*, and *pendant* gives the length; *dépenser* is spending money, not time.

examples.title: Il n'y a pas de wifi
examples.body: The hotel has a pool and no wifi: *il y a une piscine, il n'y a pas de wifi*. The negative shrinks *une* to *de*, as it has since Year 9, and *y* says *there* without repeating the hotel: *nous y allons tous les ans*. Justify the choice with a comparison and the answer has range: *je préfère le camping parce que c'est moins cher qu'un hôtel et plus près de la nature*.

steps.title: Where, with whom, for how long
steps.body:
Every holiday description answers the same questions: where you go, who with, how, for how long. The vocabulary below covers the *where* and the *who*. Two things to notice.

**Partir en vacances** is *to go on holiday*; **les vacances** is always plural in French.

**À l'étranger** means *abroad*, and it goes with *partir* or *aller*: *nous partons à l'étranger*.

visuals.fallback: Les vacances: les vacances — the holidays; partir en vacances — to go on holiday; à l'étranger — abroad; au bord de la mer — at the seaside; à la montagne — in the mountains; à la campagne — in the countryside; en ville — in town, in a city; la plage — the beach; avec ma famille — with my family; avec mes copains — with my mates; en famille — as a family; pendant deux semaines — for two weeks; une quinzaine — a fortnight; au mois d'août — in August

check.prompt: Translate into English: **nous partons à l'étranger**.
check.solution: *We go abroad.* *Partir* is to leave or go away, *à l'étranger* is abroad.
accepted: we go abroad
we are going abroad
we leave for abroad
we go away abroad
we travel abroad
we're going abroad

steps.title: En, au, aux, à: going to a place
steps.body:
*To* a country depends on the country's gender, and the exam checks it.

- **en** + feminine country: *en France, en Espagne, en Italie, en Écosse, en Angleterre*. Most countries ending in *-e* are feminine.
- **au** + masculine country: *au Portugal, au Maroc, au Canada, au pays de Galles*.
- **aux** + plural country: *aux États-Unis, aux Pays-Bas*.
- **à** + city: *à Paris, à Londres, à Lisbonne*.

*Coming from* uses **de**: *de France*, *du Portugal*, *des États-Unis*, *de Paris*.

So: *Je vais en Espagne, je reviens d'Espagne. Je vais au Maroc, je reviens du Maroc.*

visuals.alt: A table of prepositions for going to and coming from countries and cities

visuals.problem: Say where you go: Spain, Portugal, the United States, Paris

steps.text: *L'Espagne* ends in *-e* and is feminine → **en** Espagne
*Le Portugal* is masculine → **au** Portugal
*Les États-Unis* is plural → **aux** États-Unis
*Paris* is a city → **à** Paris
Coming back: *d'*Espagne, *du* Portugal, *des* États-Unis, *de* Paris

steps.title: How you get there
steps.body:
Transport takes **en** — you are *inside* it — except for the two you are not *inside*: *à vélo* and *à pied* (on foot). *En voiture, en avion, en train, en car* (coach), *en bateau*, *en métro*.

**Passer** is the verb for spending time: *nous passons deux semaines en Grèce*. Spending money is *dépenser*; mixing them up is a classic mistake.

Duration: **pendant** for how long something lasts (*pendant une semaine*), **pour** for a planned stay ahead (*je pars pour trois jours*).

visuals.fallback: Les transports et la durée: en avion — by plane; en voiture — by car; en train — by train; en car — by coach; en bateau — by boat, by ferry; à vélo — by bike; à pied — on foot; le voyage — the journey; passer une semaine — to spend a week; dépenser de l'argent — to spend money; pendant — for, during; pour — for

steps.text: *Je pars pour trois jours avec mes cousins.*

check.solution: **En car**, by coach. *En* for transport you sit inside.

steps.title: Where you stay
steps.body:
Accommodation vocabulary, and the verbs that go with it. **Loger**, **rester** and **séjourner** all mean *to stay*; **louer** is *to rent*; **réserver** is *to book*.

Watch the genders. *Un hôtel* is masculine (*un hôtel confortable*), *une auberge* is feminine, *un camping* is masculine. The gender decides the adjective ending, which is a written mark every time.

visuals.fallback: Le logement: un hôtel — a hotel; une chambre — a room; un hôtel trois étoiles — a three-star hotel; un camping — a campsite; une tente — a tent; une caravane — a caravan; une auberge de jeunesse — a youth hostel; un gîte — a self-catering cottage; une chambre d'hôtes — a bed and breakfast; un appartement de location — a rented flat; loger — to stay, to lodge; louer — to rent; réserver — to book; séjourner — to stay

accepted: un camping

steps.title: What there is, and what there isn't
steps.body: Describing the accommodation is *il y a* plus a list, and the negative is where the marks hide: after **il n'y a pas**, *un*, *une*, *du* and *des* all turn into **de**.

visuals.fallback: Ce qu'il y a: une piscine — a swimming pool; le wifi — wifi; la climatisation — air conditioning; une vue sur la mer — a sea view; un balcon — a balcony; le petit-déjeuner compris — breakfast included; la demi-pension — half board; la pension complète — full board; propre — clean; sale — dirty; bruyant — noisy; accueillant — welcoming

steps.text: *Il y a une piscine et un balcon.*
*Il n'y a pas de climatisation.*
*Il n'y a pas de wifi dans les chambres.*
*L'hôtel est propre et le personnel est accueillant.*
steps.note: adjectives agree: hôtel and personnel are masculine

check.solution: *Il n'y a pas **de** piscine.* The article disappears after the negative.

steps.title: Y: saying there
steps.body:
Once a place has been mentioned, French avoids repeating it with the pronoun **y**, *there*. It goes **before the verb**: *Nous allons en Espagne chaque été. Nous **y** allons en avion. On **y** reste deux semaines.*

With *je* it becomes *j'y*: *j'y vais tous les ans*. In the negative it stays next to the verb: *je n'y vais jamais*.

Using *y* correctly is one of the small things that marks out a Higher answer, because it shows you can handle word order.

steps.body: Write five sentences about where you normally go: the place and who with, the transport, the accommodation, one thing there is and one thing there isn't, and why you like it. Say them aloud. Then compare with the model, sentence by sentence, checking the prepositions and every *de* after a negative.

*Nous y allons en avion.*

check.prompt: Translate into French: **we go there by train**.
check.solution: *Nous **y** allons **en** train.* Two things carry the marks: **y** replaces *there* and goes **before the verb**, not after it as in English; and a means of transport you travel **in** takes **en**, so *en train*, *en voiture*, *en avion* — but **à pied** and **à vélo**, where you are not inside anything.

steps.title: Going deeper: justify, compare, and use the small words
steps.body:
A description of a holiday gets the content marks. What lifts it is **why**, **compared with what**, and accuracy in the small words.

**Justify with a comparison.** *Je préfère le camping parce que c'est moins cher qu'un hôtel et plus près de la nature.* Comparatives from last half term, put to work.

**Negatives for range.** *Nous ne partons jamais à l'étranger.* *Il n'y a plus de place en août.*

**Prepositions that are marks.** *En* Espagne, *au* Portugal, *aux* États-Unis, *du* Portugal on the way back, *en* avion, *à* vélo, *pendant* deux semaines.

**Y.** *Nous y allons chaque été* rather than repeating *en Espagne*.

**Genders decide endings.** *Un hôtel bruyant*, *une chambre propre*, *une auberge accueillante*.

steps.title: Summary
steps.body:
- **Where**: *partir en vacances*, *à l'étranger*, *au bord de la mer*, *à la montagne*, *à la campagne*.
- **To a country**: *en* (feminine), *au* (masculine), *aux* (plural), *à* (city). **From**: *de / du / des*.
- **Transport**: *en* avion, train, voiture, car, bateau; *à* vélo, *à* pied.
- **Time**: *passer deux semaines* (spend time), *pendant* (for how long), *dépenser* is for money.
- **Accommodation**: *un hôtel, un camping, une auberge de jeunesse, un gîte, une chambre d'hôtes*; verbs *loger, rester, louer, réserver*.
- **Facilities**: *il y a une piscine*; **il n'y a pas de** wifi.
- **Y** = there, before the verb: *nous y allons*.
- **Range**: comparatives with reasons, negatives, correct genders.

examTechnique.body:
Holidays and accommodation is vocabulary-heavy, and the vocabulary appears on every paper: the listening will name accommodation types and facilities, the reading will describe a hotel, the speaking role play will have you booking or describing, and the writing will ask where you go and where you stay. Learn the nouns with their genders, because the genders drive the adjective endings and the *un / une* that the marker checks.

The grammar marks are in the small words: *en / au / aux* with countries, *en* with transport, *de* after a negative, *pendant* for durations, and *y* for *there*. In writing, develop each bullet with a reason and a comparison, and use a negative for range.
examinerErrors: *À Portugal* or *en Portugal*: masculine countries take *au*.
*Il n'y a pas une piscine*: after a negative it is *pas de*.
*Une hôtel* or *un hôtel confortables*: hôtel is masculine singular.
*Je vais y* or *y je vais*: *y* sits immediately before the verb.
Listing facilities without an opinion or a reason, so the answer stays in the middle band.
examTechnique.grade9Looks: A grade 9 answer names the destination, transport and accommodation with every preposition and gender right, describes what there is and is not with il y a and il n'y a pas de, uses y to avoid repeating the place, and justifies a preference with a comparative and a reason. It adds a negative for range and, when the task reaches into the past or future, shifts tense with a signpost.
